name: Primary Bone Lymphoma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: World Health Organization (WHO) Criteria for Primary Bone Lymphoma

criteria.description: Presence of a solitary bone lesion without evidence of lymph node or visceral involvement at diagnosis
Histopathological confirmation of lymphoma in bone biopsy specimen
No evidence of systemic lymphoma or other extranodal disease at diagnosis
Radiological imaging showing lytic or mixed lytic-sclerotic bone lesion consistent with lymphoma
Immunophenotypic profile consistent with B-cell or T-cell lymphoma subtype

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of lymphoma in a solitary bone lesion without systemic involvement
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Staging workup including PET-CT and bone marrow biopsy is essential to exclude systemic lymphoma.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Localized bone pain worsening at night

common.symptomName: Pathological fracture at affected bone site
Constitutional B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
Reduced range of motion near affected bone
searchTerms: limited joint motion close to bone lesion

occasional.symptomName: Soft tissue mass adjacent to bone lesion
searchTerms: soft tissue lump next to bone lesion
tumor-like soft tissue swelling near bone
fatigue and pale skin from mild anemia

occasional.symptomName: Nerve compression symptoms if lesion near neurovascular bundle
searchTerms: symptoms from nerve pressure near vessels
nerve compression signs near neurovascular bundle
pain or numbness from nerve squeezing
high calcium symptoms like frequent urination
polyuria and mental changes due to hypercalcemia
back pain with nerve compression signs
weakness or numbness from spinal cord squeezing

rare.symptomName: Skin rash due to paraneoplastic syndrome

laboratory: Elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR) and C-reactive protein (CRP)
imaging: X-ray showing lytic or mixed lytic-sclerotic bone lesion
MRI demonstrating marrow infiltration and soft tissue extension
PET-CT showing localized increased uptake in affected bone
genetic: Clonal rearrangement of immunoglobulin or T-cell receptor genes depending on lymphoma subtype
other: Histopathology with immunohistochemistry confirming lymphoma subtype
Bone marrow biopsy negative for systemic involvement

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of infection signs (fever, elevated WBC count)
Different radiological appearance (e.g., sunburst periosteal reaction)
Lack of lymphoid markers on immunohistochemistry
Systemic symptoms related to primary tumor

redFlags: Neurological deficits indicating spinal cord or nerve compression
references: Ferreri AJM. Primary bone lymphoma. Cancer Treat Rev. 2014;40(8):1033-1041.
World Health Organization Classification of Tumours of Haematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues, 2017.
